newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec mulls law to force civil service job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Quebec mulls law to force civil service job cuts.

text.p: The Quebec government is mulling legislation to require the French-speaking Canadian province's 440,000 civil servants to accept deep job cuts, government officials said on Wednesday.

In its latest offer to the six unions representing Quebec civil servants, Quebec seeks to cut 18,675 posts through job buyouts, cutting payroll costs by C$1.4 billion. The cuts are a pivotal part of Quebec's effort to reduce its budget deficit to C$3.28 billion in 1996/97 and C$2.2 billion in 1997/98 from C$3.9 billion in 1995/96.

The government set a deadline of midnight EST Friday for reaching an agreement. Government officials are hinting at introducing special legislation forcing the unions to accept cuts when the legislature resumes sitting next Tuesday.
Under the offer, 15,000 job buyouts would be effective July 1, while 3,675 more would follow by March 31, 1998.
The public sector unions have rejected the offer, saying it went beyond the 15,000 buyouts and C$800 million of payroll cost savings agreed to in December.
"We will never agree to negotiate anything other than what was agreed to last December," the unions said in a statement.
